articles.title: Pakistan Shells Out Record Sums for Spot LNG as Qatar Supply Falters
articles.description: Pakistan is paying top dollar for LNG supply as the renewed closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the stranding of cargoes from its term supplier Qatar have forced the South Asian country to seek liquefied natural gas on the spot market. So far this month, Pakistan has issued several tenders for July delivery and is apparently willing to pay up to secure supply. In the latest tender, state-controlled importer Pakistan LNG Limited has accepted an offer from TotalEnergies Gas & Power Limited for a spot cargo for delivery on July 27-28, at a price...

articles.title: Lalbagh land row intensifies as Tejasvi Surya alleges commercial complex plan under tunnel project
articles.description: A fresh political controversy has erupted over Bengaluru's proposed Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road project, with MP Tejasvi Surya alleging that the government plans to acquire five acres of Lalbagh land for commercial development, parking and tunnel access. The state says only a small portion of the park will be used for the project. A major political controversy has emerged over the proposed Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road project after Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya alleged that the Karnataka government is planning to construct a commercial complex inside Lalbagh as part of the ambitious infrastructure project. According to Surya, the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the tunnel road mentions the construction of a commercial building and commercial parking facility along with the tunnel's entry and exit points near Lalbagh. He claimed that this information has also been placed before the Karnataka High Court through an affidavit submitted by the state government. Also Read: Wedding invitation APK scam costs Bengaluru forest officer nearly ₹10 lakh The state government has informed the High Court that only 1.9 hectares of land out of Lalbagh's total 197-hectare area will be required for the project. This works out to nearly five acres, which the government proposes to acquire for the tunnel road. However, Surya has strongly objected to the proposal, alleging that the government is effectively putting Lalbagh "up for sale." To highlight his opposition, he distributed pamphlets carrying the message that Lalbagh is being sold and urged Bengaluru residents to oppose the tunnel road project. He has also appealed to the public to raise their voice against the proposed land acquisition. The proposed tunnel road is planned between Silk Board Junction and Hebbal Junction and is one of Bengaluru's biggest infrastructure projects. The underground corridor will stretch about 16.7 kilometres and is designed to provide a fast north-south connection through the city. As per the project plan, tunnel entry and exit points are proposed near Lalbagh. The acquisition of nearly five acres is intended for these access points, commercial parking facilities and, according to the DPR, a commercial building. Also Read: Don't fall for fake medical seat promises, KEA issues strong warning to NEET aspirants The proposal has drawn objections from several organisations and members of the public, who fear that acquiring land from the historic Lalbagh Botanical Garden could affect its heritage value and damage the park's famous ancient rock formations. Despite the opposition, the government maintains that the tunnel road is expected to bring significant benefits to Bengaluru. The project aims to reduce traffic congestion in the city's central areas by creating a direct underground corridor between Hebbal and Silk Board. Officials expect the tunnel to reduce travel time between the two junctions by more than 30 minutes. The project is also intended to improve connectivity between North and South Bengaluru, strengthen links between Kempegowda International Airport and the IT corridor, reduce traffic pressure on surface roads and provide an alternative high-speed route for city commuters. The tender process for the project has already been initiated. No companies participated during the first round of bidding. In the second round, the Adani Group submitted the lowest bid. However, its bid of ₹22,267 crore is around ₹4,600 crore higher than the government's estimated project cost of ₹17,698 crore. Also Read: Street vendors to get marked spaces on Gandhi Bazaar footpaths, pedestrian access to be protected Although the bidding process was completed in December, the proposal has not yet received Cabinet approval because the quoted project cost exceeds the government's budget estimate. As the legal process and public debate continue, the future of the tunnel road project remains uncertain, with questions being raised over both its financial viability and its impact on Lalbagh, one of Bengaluru's most historic and treasured green spaces.

articles.title: Daily News Wrap-Up: POWERGRID Tenders 1 GWh Battery Storage Projects
articles.description: Power Grid Corporation of India (POWERGRID) invited bids for up to 250 MW/1,000 MWh of four-hour battery energy storage systems across India. The energy storage systems will have an operational period of up to 15 to 18 years. Bids must be submitted by August 17, 2026, for the first stage of the tender. Bids will be opened on the same day.
